## Finding that changes the lifetime explanation

The advertised engine revision `5b4e0cb0f` has a persistent renderer CPU cache. Individual transform setters/getters call `_multimesh_make_local`, allocating all instances, twelve floats each for plain 3D transforms. The cache survives dirty uploads; reallocation/free clears it. Bulk assignment does not create it, but updates it if already present. Whole-buffer readback returns a separate array without creating this cache. Motion vectors can double backing storage; no multiplier is assumed here. These are source facts, not measured binary allocations. See [official renderer source](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5b4e0cb0f/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp); local snapshot/hash in `upstream-sources.json`. Local snapshot locations: allocation/free 1537–1600, make-local 1720–1754, setter 1880+, getter 2004+, bulk 2106+, readback 2164+, dirty update 2250+.

The failed fd2 build emitted 2,235,639 grass + 30,379 flowers + 1,249 bushes = 2,267,267 base instances through individual setters. **One complete 48-byte CPU cache payload is 108,828,816 bytes (103.787 MiB)**. Patch arrays had expired, but renderer caches could still be live when finishing began. This supplies a lifetime-relevant mechanism for 645's bulk change; it does not prove its effect on physical free memory, driver allocation, or the full 4,221,042,688-byte sampled private peak. `cloudreach_pickup_readability.gd::clear_cover` returns before inspection when OFF. The failed command had no candidate argument and the config is OFF. When enabled, overlapping fields use `get_instance_transform`: even one read can recreate their caches; unchanged fields retain them. Whole-buffer reads alone have different behavior. This distinction matters to later candidate captures, but does not change the failed OFF case.
